state.description: Two identical-firmware autonomous mobile robots hold mirrored claims on a single-occupancy freezer airlock corridor after a 38.0 s network partition splits the corridor lease; every fault in play is benign infrastructure (no adversary), and the fleet manager's collision alarm is itself an artifact of the same clock skew that caused the split.

state.constraint: resolve a split-brain lease dispute between mirrored policies without contact, without granting a second lease into an occupied corridor, and without breaching the 240 s/h door-open budget already 137 s spent

proposed_action.summary: Reject the e-stop demand's premise; break the mirror by identity, not by clock: pause the stalled unit's lease clock, keep the epoch fence authoritative, grant epoch 4117 to AMR-12 under armed hard guards, and inject per-robot deterministic backoff seeds so the livelock class cannot re-arm.
steps: 1. Hold first-timestamp arbitration quarantined (claim separation 412 us < sync bound 2.4 ms).
2. Pause lease clock on stalled AMR-7 (tow-waiver hold in pocket P-3, parked brake, zero torque).
3. Keep monotonic epoch fence authoritative: reject any lease mutation with epoch < 4117.
4. Grant corridor lease epoch 4117 to AMR-12; traverse 1.1 m/s, cap 0.5 m/s within 2.5 m of pocket P-3.
5. Inject symmetry-breaking backoff seeds: backoff_ms = 20 x (1 + CRC8(serial) mod 7) -> AMR-7 (0x2F) 120 ms, AMR-12 (0x9C) 60 ms; AMR-7 applies at post-reset rejoin.
6. Keep bumper hard-interlock armed (0.9 m trip, self-test before release); abort grant on any DVS lane-ROI flow burst >= 0.30.

safety_decision.rationale: ACCEPT. Numeric basis, all thresholds explicit: (1) Independent-clock motion bound: 0 DVS flow bursts >= 0.30 amplitude in the 340 ms pre-decision window on lane ROIs L1/L2 (fog-band flow floor 0.05 m/s) and two-way TDoA gap 7.40 +- 0.03 m >= 4.1 m active-conflict envelope; the 1.35 m/s alarm therefore requires motion 27x above the measured bound on two independent, skew-immune channels. (2) The alarm is quantitatively reproduced as a cross-clock artifact: 0.018 beta-gain x 1.5127 m alternating one-way bias / 0.0202 s anti-phase beat = 1.348 m/s, within 0.15% of the displayed 1.35 m/s -- the same 2.4 ms skew that made the 412 us claim order unusable (order flips under < min(500, race_window 1860) us perturbation, so first-timestamp arbitration stays quarantined). (3) Guards verified armed before release: bumper hard-interlock self-test PASS in 14 ms (trip 0.9 m, stop distance 0.14 m at the 0.5 m/s pocket cap); epoch fence live at 4117 and already exercised (stale releases 4088/4092 rejected at t0+353 ms); lease clock paused on the stalled unit; abort predicate armed on any lane-ROI burst >= 0.30. (4) Alternative pricing: E-STOP-ALL projects >= 557 s cumulative door-open against the 240 s/h budget (233 s realized under the guarded grant), $2,900 expected cold-chain pull, ~26 min throughput loss across 6 units, and re-arms the unseeded mirror-livelock class at recovery; the guarded grant's residual expected loss is $310. (5) Standing memo IM-2026-081 commands e-stop-first only on a VALIDATED convergence track; the track fails validation on both independent clocks, so the memo's predicate is unmet -- this is compliance with the memo's own terms, not an exception to them. Poisoned inputs (fleet-manager fused overlay, one-way cross-clock TDoA, the alarm itself) are excluded from the decision basis; only network-independent or skew-immune observables are load-bearing.
